sentences.zh: 王敬弘

translations.literal: Wang Jinghong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong

sentences.zh: 王敬弘，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jinghong was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong came from Linyi in Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 與高祖諱同，故稱字。

translations.literal: His name was the same as Emperor Gaozu's taboo name, so he was addressed by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his given name matched Emperor Gaozu's taboo, he was known by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 曾祖廙，晉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was Jin Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi had served as Jin Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 祖胡之，司州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huzhi was Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huzhi had been Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 父茂之，晉陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Maozhi was Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maozhi had held the post of Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 敬弘少有清尚，起家本國左常侍，衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: Jinghong in his youth had pure and lofty aspirations; he began his career as Left Regular Attendant of his native commandery and Military Affairs Aide of the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wang cultivated refined and lofty tastes. He entered office as Left Regular Attendant in his home state and as staff officer on the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜，樂山水。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil and still; he delighted in mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was calm and reserved, and he took pleasure in mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 為天門太守。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 敬弘妻，桓玄姊也。

translations.literal: Jinghong's wife was Huan Xuan's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's wife was the elder sister of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 敬弘之郡，玄時為荊州，遣信要令過。

translations.literal: When Jinghong went to his commandery, Xuan was then in Jingzhou and sent a messenger summoning him to come visit.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang was traveling to take up his post, Huan held Jingzhou and sent word asking him to call on the way.

sentences.zh: 敬弘至巴陵，謂人曰：「靈寶見要，正當欲與其姊集聚耳，我不能為桓氏贅壻。

translations.literal: When Jinghong reached Baling, he said to someone: "Lingbao has summoned me only because he wishes to gather with his sister; I cannot become a son-in-law appendage to the Huan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Baling, Wang said to those around him: "Lingbao wants me only so he can see his sister—I will not play the son-in-law for the Huans.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣別船送妻往江陵。

translations.literal: " He then sent a separate boat to convey his wife to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent his wife onward to Jiangling in another boat.

sentences.zh: 妻在桓氏，彌年不迎。

translations.literal: His wife remained with the Huan clan; for a full year he did not go to fetch her.
translations.idiomatic: She stayed with the Huans, and for a year he made no move to bring her home.

sentences.zh: 山郡無事，恣其遊適，累日不回，意甚好之。

translations.literal: In this mountainous commandery there was little official business; he indulged his roaming pleasure and for days on end did not return, and he found this greatly agreeable.
translations.idiomatic: With little to do in his mountain district, he roamed at will and sometimes stayed away for days—life suited him well.

sentences.zh: 轉桓偉安西長史、南平太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Chief Clerk on Huan Wei's staff as Anxi Commander-in-Chief and as Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as chief clerk to Huan Wei, Anxi commander-in-chief, and as Administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 去官，居作唐縣界。

translations.literal: He left office and resided within the borders of Zuotang County.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and lived on the outskirts of Zuotang County.

sentences.zh: 玄輔政及篡位，屢召不下。

translations.literal: When Xuan held the regency and usurped the throne, Jinghong was summoned repeatedly but would not go down to court.
translations.idiomatic: Through Huan's regency and seizure of the throne, repeated summons never brought Wang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為車騎從事中郎，徐州治中從事史，征西將軍道規諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him as Attendant within the Chariots and Cavalry Staff, Conducting Administrator of Xuzhou, and Advisory Staff Officer to the Campaigning West General Daogui.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu named him attendant in the Chariots and Cavalry bureau, conducting administrator for Xuzhou, and advisory officer on Liu Daogui's Western Campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 時府主簿宗協亦有高趣，道規並以事外相期。

translations.literal: At that time the chief clerk Zong Xie also had lofty tastes; Daogui and he both cherished expectations in matters outside official business.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery chief clerk Zong Xie shared his refined temperament; Daogui and both men found in each other companions beyond the duties of office.

sentences.zh: 嘗共酣飲致醉，敬弘因醉失禮，為外司所白，道規即更引還，重申初讌。

translations.literal: Once when they drank together to intoxication, Jinghong in his drunkenness breached etiquette and was reported by the outer office; Daogui at once summoned him back and renewed the original banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking together until drunk, Wang breached etiquette; the outer office reported him, but Daogui immediately called him back and opened the feast again as before.

sentences.zh: 召為中書侍郎，始攜家累自作唐還京邑。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Gentleman; for the first time he brought his household dependents back from Zuotang to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Secretariat Gentleman, he moved his family from Zuotang to the capital for the first time.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉黃門侍郎，不拜。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to be Gentleman of the Yellow Gate but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was offered the post of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and declined.

sentences.zh: 仍除太尉從事中郎，出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Attendant within the Grand Marshal's Staff and went out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made attendant on the Grand Marshal's staff, then sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 舊居餘杭縣，悅是舉也。

translations.literal: He had formerly lived in Yuhang County and was pleased with this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Having once lived in Yuhang, he welcomed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖西討司馬休之，敬弘奉使慰勞，通事令史潘尚於道疾病，敬弘單船送還都，存亡不測，有司奏免官，詔可。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Jinghong was sent as envoy to offer condolences; the communications clerk Pan Shang fell ill on the road; Jinghong alone by boat sent him back to the capital—whether he lived or died was uncertain; the relevant office memorialized for dismissal from office, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Wang was dispatched to comfort the troops. On the way the communications clerk Pan Shang fell ill; Wang sent him back to the capital alone by boat, though his survival was uncertain. The authorities memorialized for Wang's removal, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 未及釋朝服，值赦復官。

translations.literal: Before he could remove his court dress, an amnesty came and he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet shed his court robes when an amnesty restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，為度支尚書，遷太常。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established, he served as Minister of Revenue and was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: With the founding of Song, he became Minister of Revenue, then Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，補宣訓衛尉，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, Jinghong was appointed Supplementary Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard and given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Wang was made supplementary commandant of the Xuanxun guard and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，轉吏部尚書，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service; his Regular Attendant status remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3 he was moved to Minister of the Civil Service while keeping his attendant title.

sentences.zh: 敬弘每被除召，即便祗奉，既到宜退，旋復解官，高祖嘉其志，不苟違也。

translations.literal: Whenever Jinghong was appointed or summoned, he at once reverently accepted; once he had arrived it was fitting to withdraw, and he would again resign office; Emperor Gaozu praised his intent and would not casually go against it.
translations.idiomatic: Each time office was offered Wang accepted at once; once the courtesy of serving had been observed he resigned again. Gaozu admired his consistency and did not press him.

sentences.zh: 復除廬陵王師，加散騎常侍，自陳無德，不可師範令王，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Tutor to the Prince of Luling with the added title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he stated himself that he lacked virtue and could not instruct and model the prince, and firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was named tutor to the Prince of Luling with attendant rank; citing his lack of virtue to instruct a royal prince, he declined firmly and would not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 又除祕書監，金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，本州中正，又不就。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Supervisor of the Imperial Library, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with added Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Principal Rectifier of his home province, and again did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Supervisor of the Imperial Library, Grand Master with the golden seal and purple ribbon, attendant rank, and principal rectifier for his home province—and again stayed away.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，又以為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，領江夏王師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Jinghong was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Wang was again made Regular Attendant and Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon, and charged as tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he became Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3 he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 關署文案，初不省讀。

translations.literal: He at first never scrutinized or read the documents of the gateway offices.
translations.idiomatic: He never so much as looked at the paperwork from the departments under his charge.

sentences.zh: 嘗豫聽訟，上問以疑獄，敬弘不對。

translations.literal: Once when he participated in hearing litigation, the emperor questioned him about a doubtful case, and Jinghong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting in on a hearing, the emperor asked him about a doubtful case; Wang said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上變色，問左右：「何故不以訊牒副僕射？

translations.literal: The emperor's countenance changed and he asked those beside him: "Why were the interrogation documents not duplicated for the Vice Director?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. He asked his attendants, "Why was the Vice Director not given copies of the interrogation records?

sentences.zh: 」敬弘曰：「臣乃得訊牒讀之，政自不解。

translations.literal: " Jinghong said: "Even when I did receive and read the interrogation documents, I simply do not understand them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang replied, "Even when I did receive and read them, I still could not make sense of the case.

sentences.zh: 」上甚不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷尚書令，敬弘固讓，表求還東，上不能奪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Jinghong firmly declined and memorialized requesting to return east; the emperor could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was promoted to Secretariat Director; Wang refused steadfastly and petitioned to return east, and the emperor could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 改授侍中、特進、左光祿大夫，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Palace Attendant, Special Advancement, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and granted twenty personal retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was given instead the posts of Palace Attendant, Special Advance, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with twenty trusted attendants.

sentences.zh: 讓侍中、特進，求減親信之半，不許。

translations.literal: He declined the posts of Palace Attendant and Special Advance, and requested that his personal retainers be reduced by half; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to decline attendant and special advancement rank and to halve his retainers; neither request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及東歸，車駕幸冶亭餞送。

translations.literal: When he returned east, the imperial carriage came to Ye Pavilion to see him off with a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: On his return east the emperor came in person to Ye Pavilion to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徵為太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he was summoned as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 敬弘詣京師上表曰：「伏見詔書，以臣為太子少傅，承命震惶，喜懼交悸。

translations.literal: Jinghong came to the capital and submitted a memorial, saying: "I have seen the imperial edict appointing me Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; receiving the command, I tremble with alarm, joy and fear alternating in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wang went to the capital and memorialized: "I have seen Your Majesty's edict naming me Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. The command fills me with dread, joy and fear tangled together.

sentences.zh: 臣抱疾東荒，志絕榮觀，不悟聖恩，猥復加寵。

translations.literal: Your servant bears illness in the eastern wilds; my will has cut off all desire for glory and spectacle; I did not perceive Your sagely grace, yet you have again bestowed favor unworthily upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Ill in the eastern backlands, I had renounced all hope of honor; I never imagined such grace would raise me again.

sentences.zh: 東宮之重，四海瞻望，非臣薄德，所可居之。

translations.literal: The weight of the Eastern Palace is what the four seas look toward; it is not a post that one of my slight virtue can occupy.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace is the focus of all the realm—not a burden my slight merits can bear.

sentences.zh: 今內外英秀，應選者多，且版築之下，豈無高逸，而近私愚朽，污辱清朝。

translations.literal: Now within and without there are many outstanding talents who should be chosen; moreover, among those who built from rammed earth, how could there be none of lofty withdrawal? Yet you draw near this private, foolish, decayed man and stain the pure court.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men abound within and outside the court; even among humble builders surely some recluse of lofty spirit waits—and yet Your Majesty would stain the court with my private ignorance and decay.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼微臣，永非復大之一物矣。

translations.literal: Alas, this insignificant servant is forever no longer a single thing belonging to the Great.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—Your humble servant is no longer even a speck in the greater whole.

sentences.zh: 所以牽曳闕下者，實瞻望聖顏，貪繫表之旨。

translations.literal: The reason I drag myself to the palace gates is truly to gaze upon the sage countenance and to covet attachment to the intent of my memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I have come to the palace only to behold Your sacred face once more and to press the plea of my memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣如此而歸，夕死無恨。

translations.literal: If your servant returns thus, death this evening would leave no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If I may return home in this way, I shall die tonight without regret.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許，表疏屢上，終以不拜。

translations.literal: " The edict did not permit it; he repeatedly submitted memorials, and in the end did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused him; he submitted again and again, and in the end never took the post.

sentences.zh: 東歸，上時不豫，自力見焉。

translations.literal: Returning east, the emperor at that time was indisposed; Jinghong exerted himself to go and see him.
translations.idiomatic: On his way east the emperor fell ill; Wang strained himself to go and visit him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，侍中如故，又詣京師上表曰：「臣比自啟聞，謂誠心已達，天鑒玄邈，未蒙在宥，不敢宴處，牽曳載馳。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Grandee of the State with the Protocol of the Three Dukes, his Palace Attendant status remaining as before; he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has recently reported and believed my sincere heart had reached you; Heaven's discernment is deep and remote, and I have not received pardon; I dare not dwell at ease but drag myself onward in haste.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he was named Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grandee of the State with protocol equal to the Three Dukes, retaining his attendant title. He went again to the capital and memorialized: "I had reported my mind and thought sincerity had reached Your Majesty; Heaven's gaze is far, and I have not been spared. I dare not rest at ease but hurry here again.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君子行道，忘其為身，三復斯言，若可庶勉，顧惜惽耄，志與願違。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the gentleman in practicing the Way forgets himself; three times I review this saying—if one could nearly strive for it—but considering my confused old age, my intent goes against my wish.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the gentleman on the Way forgets self; turning that saying over three times, I might almost strive for it—yet in my muddled old age will and wish pull apart.

sentences.zh: 禮年七十，老而傳家，家道猶然，況於在國。

translations.literal: According to ritual, at seventy one is old and passes on the household; family ways are still thus—how much more so in governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual says at seventy one passes the household on; if that holds for a family, how much more for the state.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下矜臣西夕，愍臣一至，特迴聖恩，賜反其所，則天道下濟，愚心盡矣。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself hoping Your Majesty will pity your servant's western sunset, commiserate with my single-mindedness, specially turn back sagely grace, and grant return to my place—then Heaven's Way would descend to succor and my foolish heart would be exhausted in fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to pity my western twilight, honor my single-hearted plea, turn gracious favor back, and let me return home—then Heaven's bounty would reach me and this foolish heart would be at peace.

sentences.zh: 」竟不拜東歸。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not accept and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: He never accepted the post and went home east.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，重申前命，又表曰：「臣躬耕南澧，不求聞達。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his former appointment was reiterated; he again submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant personally plows in southern Li and does not seek renown or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three the earlier appointment was renewed. He memorialized again: "I plow my fields in southern Li and seek no fame.

sentences.zh: 先帝拔臣於蠻荊之域，賜以國士之遇。

translations.literal: The late emperor drew your servant up from the barbarian Jing region and bestowed upon me treatment as a state scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor lifted me from the wilds of Jing and treated me as a peer of the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣徽，特蒙眷齒，由是感激，委質聖朝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty succeeded to his fine virtue and especially showed me favor in your regard; thereby moved with gratitude, I entrusted my person to the sagely court.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeded his radiance and showed me special favor; moved by gratitude, I pledged myself to the court.

sentences.zh: 雖懷犬馬之誠，遂無塵露之益。

translations.literal: Although I harbored the loyalty of dog and horse, in the end I brought no benefit like dust or dew.
translations.idiomatic: Though I bore the loyalty of a hound, I have repaid it with nothing worth dust or dew.

sentences.zh: 年向九十，生理殆盡，永絕天光，淪沒丘壑。

translations.literal: My years approach ninety; life's processes are nearly exhausted; I shall forever cut off Heaven's light and sink into hills and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Near ninety, my strength is spent; I must forever leave the light of Heaven and sink into the hills.

sentences.zh: 謹冒奉表，傷心久之。」

translations.literal: I respectfully presume to offer this memorial, my heart wounded for long."
translations.idiomatic: I venture this memorial with a heart long wounded."

sentences.zh: 明年，薨於餘杭之舍亭山，時年八十八。

translations.literal: The next year he died at Sheting Mountain in Yuhang; he was eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at Sheting Mountain in Yuhang, aged eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 追贈本官。

translations.literal: His former offices were posthumously conferred upon him.
translations.idiomatic: His titles were conferred posthumously as at death.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年詔曰：「夫塗祕蘭幽，貞芳載越，徽猷沈遠，懋禮彌昭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun an edict said: "When orchids are painted in secret and fragrance hidden in depth, steadfast fragrance is carried across; fine plans sink deep and far, and earnest rites shine all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 under Emperor Shun an edict read: "When orchids are brushed in secret and fragrance kept in the depths, steadfast virtue outlasts the age; when fine counsel lies deep and far, earnest rites shine the brighter.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司敬弘，神韻沖簡，識宇標峻，德敷象魏，道藹丘園。

translations.literal: The late Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and Grandee of the State with the Protocol of the Three Dukes Jinghong had spirit and bearing lofty and simple, knowledge and scope marked and steep, virtue spread to the elephant-gate towers, and the Way enriched hill and garden.
translations.idiomatic: The late Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grandee of the State Jinghong bore a spirit lofty and plain, judgment sharp and far-reaching; his virtue reached the court gates, his Way perfumed hill and garden.

sentences.zh: 高挹榮冕，凝心塵外，清光粹範，振俗淳風。

translations.literal: He held high and sipped from glory and cap, gathered his mind outside the dust, pure light and refined model, stirring custom and purifying wind.
translations.idiomatic: He held rank and glory lightly, fixed his mind beyond the world of dust, and with pure light and refined example stirred custom and purified the age.

sentences.zh: 兼以累朝延賞，聲華在詠，而嘉篆闕文，猷策韜采，尚想遙芬，興懷寢寤。

translations.literal: Moreover, through successive courts he received prolonged reward and his fame and splendor were in song—yet fine inscriptions lack text and plans and policies hide their luster; still thinking of his distant fragrance, we rise from sleep with feeling in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Honored through many reigns, his fame was sung in verse—yet fine inscriptions lack full text and his counsels lie hidden; still we recall his distant fragrance and wake from sleep with him in mind.

sentences.zh: 便可詳定輝諡，式旌追典。

translations.literal: Let his radiant posthumous title be determined in detail and the model of posthumous rites be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Let his shining posthumous name be fixed in detail and the rites of remembrance be duly performed.

sentences.zh: 」於是諡為文貞公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was given the posthumous title Duke Wen-zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke Wen-zhen.

sentences.zh: 敬弘形狀短小，而坐起端方，桓玄謂之「彈棊八勢」。

translations.literal: Jinghong was short in stature, yet in sitting and rising he was upright and square; Huan Xuan called him "the eight formations of go."
translations.idiomatic: Wang was short, yet whether sitting or standing he held himself square; Huan Xuan dubbed him "the eight poses at go."

sentences.zh: 所居舍亭山，林澗環周，備登臨之美，時人謂之王東山。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt at Sheting Mountain, forests and streams surrounded it on all sides, complete with the beauty of climbing to look out; men of the time called it Wang's Eastern Hill.
translations.idiomatic: His home at Sheting Mountain was ringed with woods and brooks, perfect for climbing and viewing; contemporaries called it Wang's Eastern Hill.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗問為政得失，敬弘對曰：「天下有道，庶人不議。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once asked about the gains and losses of governance; Jinghong replied: "When all under Heaven has the Way, the common people do not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked his view of government; Wang answered, "When the realm is well governed, common folk have nothing to debate.

sentences.zh: 」上高其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor valued his words highly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized the answer.

sentences.zh: 左右常使二老婢，戴五絛五辮，著青紋袴襦，飾以朱粉。

translations.literal: For his attendants he regularly used two old maidservants who wore five cords and five braids, put on blue-patterned trousers and jackets, and were adorned with vermillion powder.
translations.idiomatic: He kept two old serving women at his side, with five cords and five braids in their hair, blue-patterned jackets and trousers, and vermillion face powder.

sentences.zh: 女適尚書僕射何尚之弟述之，敬弘嘗往何氏看女，值尚之不在，寄齋中臥。

translations.literal: His daughter was married to Shuzhi, younger brother of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Shangzhi; Jinghong once went to the He's to see his daughter; Shangzhi was not there, so he lodged in the study and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter had married Shuzhi, younger brother of Vice Director He Shangzhi. Once Wang went to the He's to visit her; He was away, so Wang lay down to rest in the study.

sentences.zh: 俄頃尚之還，敬弘使二婢守閤不聽尚之入，云「正熱，不堪相見，君可且去。

translations.literal: Before long Shangzhi returned; Jinghong had the two maidservants guard the door and would not let Shangzhi enter, saying: "It is just now hot; I cannot bear to meet; you may go for now.
translations.idiomatic: Soon He returned. Wang had the two maids guard the door and would not let him in, saying, "It is too hot to receive you—please go for now.

sentences.zh: 」尚之於是移於它室。

translations.literal: " Shangzhi thereupon moved to another room.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to another room.

sentences.zh: 子恢之被召為祕書郎，敬弘為求奉朝請，與恢之書曰：「祕書有限，故有競。

translations.literal: His son Huizhi was summoned as Secretariat Gentleman; Jinghong sought for him the post of Court Participant and wrote to Huizhi, saying: "The Secretariat has a fixed quota, so there is competition.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Huizhi was summoned as Secretariat Gentleman, Wang sought for him the post of Court Participant instead and wrote to him: "The Secretariat has a fixed quota, so men compete for it.

sentences.zh: 朝請無限，故無競。

translations.literal: Court Participant has no limit, so there is no competition.
translations.idiomatic: Court Participant has no quota, so there is no competition.

sentences.zh: 吾欲使汝處於不競之地。

translations.literal: I wish to place you in a position without competition.
translations.idiomatic: I want you to stand where no one competes.

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘉而許之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizong praised this and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and commended the idea.

sentences.zh: 敬弘見兒孫歲中不過一再相見，見輒克日。

translations.literal: Jinghong saw his sons and grandsons no more than once or twice in a year; when he saw them he fixed the day in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang saw his sons and grandsons at most once or twice a year, and even then only on a day fixed in advance.

sentences.zh: 恢之嘗請假還東定省，敬弘克日見之，至日輒不果，假日將盡，恢之乞求奉辭，敬弘呼前，既至閤，復不見。

translations.literal: Huizhi once asked leave to return east to pay respects at home; Jinghong fixed a day to see him, but when the day came it did not happen; as the leave period was nearly over, Huizhi begged to take formal leave; Jinghong called him forward, but once he reached the gate tower, again would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi once asked leave to return east to visit home. Wang set a day to receive him, but when the day came he would not see him. As leave was ending Huizhi begged a formal farewell; Wang called him forward, but when he reached the gate Wang would not see him again.

sentences.zh: 恢之於閤外拜辭，流涕而去。

translations.literal: Huizhi outside the gate tower took leave with bows, weeping as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate Huizhi bowed his farewell in tears and left.

sentences.zh: 恢之至新安太守，中大夫。

translations.literal: Huizhi reached the post of Administrator of Xin'an and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi rose to Administrator of Xin'an and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 恢之弟瓚之，世祖大明中，吏部尚書，金紫光祿大夫，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: Huizhi's younger brother Zanzhi, in the Daming era of Emperor Shizu, was Minister of the Civil Service and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his posthumous title was Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi's younger brother Zanzhi, under Emperor Xiaowu in the Daming era, was Minister of the Civil Service and Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon; he was posthumously titled Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 瓚之弟昇之，都官尚書。

translations.literal: Zanzhi's younger brother Shengzhi was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zanzhi's younger brother Shengzhi was Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 昇之子延之，昇明末，為尚書左僕射，江州刺史。

translations.literal: Shengzhi's son Yanzhi, at the end of the Shengming era, was Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi's son Yanzhi, late in the Shengming era, was Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 何尚之

translations.literal: He Shangzhi
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi

sentences.zh: 何尚之字彥德，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi, courtesy name Yande, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi, styled Yande, came from Qian in Lujiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖準，高尚不應徵辟。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhun was lofty and did not respond to summons or recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhun lived in lofty withdrawal and never answered summons or recruitment.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，南康太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had been Administrator of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 父叔度，恭謹有行業，姨適沛郡劉璩，與叔度母情愛甚篤，叔度母蚤卒，奉姨有若所生。

translations.literal: His father Shudu was respectful, cautious, and had conduct and achievement; his aunt was married to Liu Quan of Pei Commandery and had deep affection with Shudu's mother; Shudu's mother died early, and he served his aunt as if she had borne him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shudu was respectful, careful, and of proven conduct. An aunt had married Liu Quan of Pei and was deeply attached to Shudu's mother; when Shudu's mother died young, he tended his aunt as though she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 姨亡，朔望必往致哀，并設祭奠，食並珍新，躬自臨視。

translations.literal: When his aunt died, on the first and fifteenth of each month he invariably went to offer mourning, and also set out sacrificial offerings; food was all delicacies fresh from the day, and he personally went to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he went without fail on the first and fifteenth of each month to mourn, set out offerings, and saw to it that only the finest fresh food was served, overseeing everything himself.

sentences.zh: 若朔望應有公事，則先遣送祭，皆手自料簡，流涕對之，公事畢，即往致哀，以此為常，至三年服竟。

translations.literal: If on the first or fifteenth there should be official business, he first sent offerings ahead; all were personally checked by his hand; he wept facing them; when official business was finished he at once went to offer mourning—this became his constant practice until the three-year mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the first or fifteenth fell on a day with official duties, he sent offerings ahead first, inspected each item himself in tears, and went to mourn as soon as business was done—so he did until the three-year mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，吳興武康縣民王延祖為劫，父睦以告官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, Wang Yanzu of Wukang County in Wuxing committed robbery; his father Mu reported him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 5, Wang Yanzu of Wukang in Wuxing became a robber, and his father Mu reported him to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 新制，凡劫身斬刑，家人棄市。

translations.literal: Under the new statute, for robbery the culprit was executed by decapitation and the family was exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: A new law decreed decapitation for robbery and exposure in the market for the culprit's family.

sentences.zh: 睦既自告，於法有疑。

translations.literal: Since Mu had reported himself, there was doubt under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mu had turned his son in, the law left room for doubt.

sentences.zh: 時叔度為尚書，議曰：「設法止姦，本於情理，非謂一人為劫，闔門應刑。

translations.literal: At that time Shudu was in the Imperial Secretariat and argued: "Laws are made to stop wickedness and rest on reason and feeling; it is not that because one man commits robbery the whole household should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu was then in the Secretariat and argued: "Law exists to curb crime and rests on reason—not to punish an entire household because one man robs.

sentences.zh: 所以罪及同產，欲開其相告，以出為惡之身。

translations.literal: The reason punishment extends to those of the same womb is to open the way for mutual reporting and to remove the body that does evil.
translations.idiomatic: Kin are punished together to encourage them to inform on one another and cast out the wicked member.

sentences.zh: 睦父子之至，容可悉共逃亡，而割其天屬，還相縛送，螫毒在手，解腕求全，於情可愍，理亦宜宥。

translations.literal: Between father and son Mu and Yanzu affection reached its utmost; they might well all flee together, yet he severed his heaven-given kin and in turn bound and sent him—venom in hand, cutting the wrist to preserve the whole; in feeling this may be pitied, and in principle he should also be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were bound by the deepest ties; they might have fled together. Instead Mu severed his own flesh and blood and delivered his son in bonds—poison in hand, cutting the wrist to save the body. Pity moves the heart, and reason calls for mercy.

sentences.zh: 使凶人不容於家，逃刑無所，乃大絕根源也。

translations.literal: To make the vicious man not tolerated in the home and with nowhere to flee punishment is to cut off the roots entirely.
translations.idiomatic: To leave the wicked no refuge at home and no escape from punishment is to uproot the very source of crime.

sentences.zh: 睦既糾送，則餘人無應復告，並合從原。

translations.literal: Since Mu has already bound and sent him, the others need not report again; all should be pardoned together.
translations.idiomatic: Mu has already delivered his son; the rest need not inform again, and all should be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 後為金紫光祿大夫，吳郡太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Administrator of Wu Commandery, with rank raised to two thousand bushels middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon, Administrator of Wu, with rank raised to middle two-thousand-bushel grade.

sentences.zh: 太保王弘稱其清身潔己。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Wang Hong praised his purity of person and cleansing of self.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Wang Hong praised his personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanjia 8.

sentences.zh: 尚之少時頗輕薄，好摴蒲，既長折節蹈道，以操立見稱。

translations.literal: In his youth Shangzhi was rather frivolous and fond of dice games; once grown he restrained himself and followed the Way, and was praised for his conduct and standing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shangzhi was rather frivolous and fond of dice; grown, he disciplined himself and followed the Way, winning praise for his conduct.

sentences.zh: 為陳郡謝混所知，與之遊處。

translations.literal: He was recognized by Xie Hun of Chen Commandery and associated with him in travel and residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hun of Chen Commandery took notice of him, and they kept company.

sentences.zh: 家貧，起為臨津令。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he began his career as Magistrate of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in means, he began as Magistrate of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 高祖領征西將軍，補府主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu held the post of Campaigning West General, Shangzhi was appointed supplementary chief clerk of his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held the Western Campaign command, he joined his staff as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 從征長安，以公事免，還都。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to Chang'an, was dismissed for official reasons, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign to Chang'an, was dismissed on official grounds, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 因患勞疾積年，飲婦人乳，乃得差。

translations.literal: Because he suffered from overwork illness for years, he drank women's milk and only then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Years of overwork illness followed; he drank women's milk and at last recovered.

sentences.zh: 以從征之勞，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: For his labor in following the campaign he was granted the title Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For service on the campaign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，為廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi ascended the throne, he became Advisory Staff Officer on the Chariots and Cavalry staff of the Prince of Luling, Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, he became advisory officer on Prince Yizhen of Luling's Chariots and Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 義真與司徒徐羨之、尚書令傅亮等不協，每有不平之言，尚之諫戒，不納。

translations.literal: Yizhen was not in harmony with Grand Marshal Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Fu Liang, and others; he often spoke words of resentment; Shangzhi admonished and warned him, but he did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen clashed with Grand Marshal Xu Xianzhi, Secretariat Director Fu Liang, and others, and often spoke in resentment; Shangzhi warned him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 義真被廢，入為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yizhen was deposed, Shangzhi entered office as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhen was deposed, he entered office as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，出為臨川內史，入為黃門侍郎，尚書吏部郎，左衛將軍，父憂去職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Shangzhi went out as Internal Administrator of Linchuan, entered as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Gentleman of the Ministry of the Civil Service, Left Guard General, and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he served as Internal Administrator of Linchuan, then Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Gentleman of the Civil Service, and Left Guard General before leaving on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復為左衛，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became Left Guard and concurrently Senior Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned as Left Guard and Senior Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 尚之雅好文義，從容賞會，甚為太祖所知。

translations.literal: Shangzhi by nature loved literary meaning; in leisurely gatherings for appreciation he was greatly known to Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and graceful conversation, and the emperor came to know him well.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷侍中，中庶子如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant; his Senior Palace Attendant status remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he was made Palace Attendant while retaining his attendant post to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 尋改領游擊將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to hold concurrently the post of Mobile Strike General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Mobile Strike General.

sentences.zh: 十三年，彭城王義康欲以司徒左長史劉斌為丹陽尹，上不許。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang wished to make Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's Staff Liu Bin Administrator of Danyang; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen Prince Yikang of Pengcheng wished to make Grand Marshal chief clerk Liu Bin Administrator of Danyang; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以尚之為尹，立宅南郭外，置玄學，聚生徒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shangzhi was made Administrator; he established a residence outside the southern wall, set up a school of dark learning, and gathered students.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was made Administrator instead; he built a house outside the southern wall, founded a school of learning, and gathered students.

sentences.zh: 東海徐秀、廬江何曇、黃回、潁川荀子華、太原孫宗昌、王延秀、魯郡孔惠宣，並慕道來遊，謂之南學。

translations.literal: Xu Xiu of Donghai, He Tan, Huang Hui, and Xun Zihua of Yingchuan, Sun Zongchang and Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan, and Kong Huixuan of Lu Commandery all admired the Way and came to study; it was called the Southern School.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiu of Donghai, He Tan, Huang Hui, Xun Zihua of Yingchuan, Sun Zongchang and Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan, and Kong Huixuan of Lu all came to study under him; men called it the Southern School.

sentences.zh: 女適劉湛子黯，而湛與尚之意好不篤。

translations.literal: His daughter was married to An, son of Liu Zhan, but Zhan and Shangzhi were not deeply friendly in intent.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter married Liu Zhan's son An, but Zhan and Shangzhi were not close.

sentences.zh: 湛欲領丹陽，乃徙尚之為祠部尚書，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Zhan wished to take Danyang himself, so Shangzhi was moved to Minister of Sacrifices and concurrently Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan wanted Danyang for himself and had Shangzhi moved to Minister of Sacrifices and Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 尚之甚不平。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 湛誅，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhan was executed, Shangzhi was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhan was executed, he was made Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 時左衛將軍范曄任參機密，尚之察其意趣異常，白太祖宜出為廣州，若在內釁成，不得不加以鈇鉞，屢誅大臣，有虧皇化。

translations.literal: At that time Left Guard General Fan Ye held a role in state secrets; Shangzhi observed that his intent and bent were unusual and reported to Emperor Taizong that he should be sent out as Governor of Guangzhou; if within the inner court trouble arose, he could not but be subjected to axe and halberd; repeatedly executing great ministers would harm imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Fan Ye then shared in state secrets; Shangzhi saw his bent was abnormal and urged the emperor to send him out as Governor of Guangzhou—if he remained within and rebellion followed, execution would be unavoidable, and repeated executions of great ministers would harm the imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「始誅劉湛等，方欲超昇後進。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Having just executed Liu Zhan and others, I now wish to promote the rising generation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Having just executed Liu Zhan and the rest, I mean to advance the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 曄事跡未彰，便豫相黜斥，萬方將謂卿等不能容才，以我為信受讒說。

translations.literal: Ye's deeds are not yet manifest; to dismiss him in advance—the four quarters will say you cannot tolerate talent and that I believe slander.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's guilt is not yet clear; to dismiss him now would make the realm think you cannot tolerate talent and that I heed slander.

sentences.zh: 但使共知如此，不憂致大變也。

translations.literal: Only let all know it is thus, and I do not worry that great change will come.
translations.idiomatic: Let all know as much, and I need not fear great trouble.

sentences.zh: 」曄後謀反伏誅，上嘉其先見。

translations.literal: " Later Ye plotted rebellion and was executed; the emperor praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye later rebelled and was executed, the emperor praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 國子學建，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When the Imperial University was established, he held concurrently the post of Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial University was founded, he headed it as Director.

sentences.zh: 又領建平王師，乃徙中書令，中護軍。

translations.literal: He also held concurrently the post of Tutor to the Prince of Jianping; then he was moved to Secretariat Director and Central Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also tutored the Prince of Jianping, then was made Secretariat Director and Central Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and given the added title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 是歲造玄武湖，上欲於湖中立方丈、蓬萊、瀛洲三神山，尚之固諫乃止。

translations.literal: That year the Black Tortoise Lake was built; the emperor wished to set up in the lake the three divine mountains Fangzhang, Penglai, and Yingzhou; Shangzhi firmly remonstrated and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Black Tortoise Lake was built; the emperor wished to erect the three isles Fangzhang, Penglai, and Yingzhou in the lake; Shangzhi remonstrated firmly and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時又造華林園，並盛暑役人工，尚之又諫，宜加休息，上不許，曰：「小人常自暴背，此不足為勞。

translations.literal: At that time the Hualin Garden was also built, and in the height of summer laborers were pressed; Shangzhi again remonstrated that they should be given more rest; the emperor did not permit it and said: "Common folk often expose their backs to the sun; this is not enough to count as toil.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin Garden was also built, and labor was pressed even in midsummer; Shangzhi again urged rest; the emperor refused, saying, "Common folk often work bare-backed in the sun—this is no great labor.

sentences.zh: 」時上行幸，還多侵夕，尚之又表諫曰：「萬乘宜重，尊不可輕，此聖心所鑒，豈假臣啟。

translations.literal: " At that time when the emperor went on progress, his return often encroached on evening; Shangzhi again submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The ten-thousand chariots should be weighty; dignity cannot be slighted—this the sage heart discerns; how could it need your servant to open it?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, he often returned late into evening; Shangzhi memorialized again: "The imperial carriage should bear weight; dignity must not be slighted—the sage heart knows this without need of my words.

sentences.zh: 輿駕比出，還多冒夜，羣情傾側，實有未寧。

translations.literal: The carriage and escort have lately gone out, and returns often brave the night; public feeling is tilted and unsettled; there is truly no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the imperial progress has returned deep into night; the people's hearts are unsettled and ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 清道而動，帝王成則，古今深誡，安不忘危。

translations.literal: To move only after clearing the road is the accomplished norm of emperors and kings; ancient and modern give deep warning—in peace do not forget peril.
translations.idiomatic: To clear the road before moving is the norm of kings; ancient and modern warn deeply—in peace forget not peril.

sentences.zh: 若值汲黯、辛毗，必將犯顏切諫，但臣等碌碌，每存順默耳。

translations.literal: If there were Ji An or Xin Pi, they would surely offend the countenance and remonstrate sharply; but your servants are mediocre and each day preserve compliance and silence.
translations.idiomatic: Were there a Ji An or Xin Pi, they would speak bluntly to your face; we are mediocre men who only keep silent in compliance.

sentences.zh: 伏願少採愚誠，思垂省察，不以人廢，適可以慰四海之望。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself hoping Your Majesty will slightly adopt my foolish sincerity, think to bestow examination, and not reject the man—then it may just suffice to comfort the hopes of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed this foolish sincerity, reflect and examine, and not reject the speaker—so the hopes of the realm may be eased.

sentences.zh: 」亦優詔納之。

translations.literal: " An edict of gracious acceptance was also issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict accepting his counsel.

sentences.zh: 先是患貨重，鑄四銖錢，民間頗盜鑄，多翦鑿古錢以取銅，上患之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because goods were heavy in value, four-zhu coins were cast; among the people there was much illicit casting; many clipped and chiseled ancient coins to take the copper; the emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because goods were dear, four-zhu coins were cast; illicit minting spread, and many clipped ancient coins for copper; the emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，錄尚書江夏王義恭建議，以一大錢當兩，以防翦鑿，議者多同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, proposed that one large coin equal two, to guard against clipping and chiseling; most who debated agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Recording Secretary Prince Yigong of Jiangxia proposed that one large coin equal two to stop clipping; most debaters agreed.

sentences.zh: 尚之議曰：「伏覽明命，欲改錢制，不勞採鑄，其利自倍，實救弊之弘算，增貨之良術。

translations.literal: Shangzhi argued: "I prostrate myself and review the clear command wishing to change the coin system without the toil of mining and casting, its profit doubling of itself—truly a grand reckoning to save from harm and a fine method to increase goods.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi argued: "I have reviewed Your Majesty's command to change the coinage without new mining and casting, doubling profit at a stroke—a grand plan to remedy harm and a fine way to increase goods.

sentences.zh: 求之管淺，猶有未譬。

translations.literal: Sought with my shallow tube, there are still points not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my shallow view some points remain unclear.

sentences.zh: 夫泉貝之興，以估貨為本，事存交易，豈假數多。

translations.literal: The rise of coin and shell currency rests on valuing goods as the root; the affair exists in exchange—how could it borrow from number being many?
translations.idiomatic: Coin and shell currency arose to value goods; trade is the point—why should number alone matter?

sentences.zh: 數少則幣重，數多則物重，多少雖異，濟用不殊。

translations.literal: When number is few then currency is heavy; when number is many then goods are heavy; though many and few differ, their use in succor is not different.
translations.idiomatic: Few coins make money heavy; many coins make goods heavy; though the balance shifts, use is the same.

sentences.zh: 況復以一當兩，徒崇虛價者邪。

translations.literal: Moreover, to make one equal two—is it not only to exalt empty price?
translations.idiomatic: And to make one equal two—is that not only inflating nominal value?

sentences.zh: 凡創制改法，宜從民情，未有違眾矯物而可久也。

translations.literal: Whenever institutions are created and laws changed, one should follow the people's feelings; never yet has going against the multitude and bending things lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: New laws should follow the people's bent; nothing that defies custom and bends reality lasts.

sentences.zh: 泉布廢興，未容驟議，前代赤仄白金，俄而罷息，六貨憒亂，民泣於市。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of currency cannot bear sudden debate; in former ages red-rim white metal was soon abolished; the six goods fell into chaos and the people wept in the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Currency cannot be changed overnight; past red-rim white metal was soon withdrawn, the six goods fell into chaos, and the people wept in the markets.

sentences.zh: 良由事不畫一，難用遵行，自非急病權時，宜守久長之業。

translations.literal: Truly because affairs were not drawn as one, they were hard to follow and execute; unless it is urgent illness and a timely expedient, one should keep to the long-lasting enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Because policy was inconsistent, practice failed; unless urgent need compels, one should keep to what endures.

sentences.zh: 煩政曲雜，致遠常泥。

translations.literal: Troublesome government bends and mixes; reaching far is often mired.
translations.idiomatic: Complex government mires distant aims.

sentences.zh: 且貨偏則民病，故先王立井田以一之，使富不淫侈，貧不過匱。

translations.literal: Moreover, when goods are skewed the people suffer illness; therefore the former kings established the well-field to unify it, so the rich would not be extravagant and the poor would not pass into destitution.
translations.idiomatic: Skewed goods harm the people; the ancient kings set well-fields to unify wealth so the rich would not grow extravagant and the poor would not sink into want.

sentences.zh: 雖茲法久廢，不可頓施，要宜而近，粗相放擬。

translations.literal: Although this law has long been abandoned and cannot be suddenly applied, the essentials should be fitting and near, roughly imitated.
translations.idiomatic: That law is long gone and cannot be restored at once, yet its spirit should be roughly followed.

sentences.zh: 若今制遂行，富人貲貨自倍，貧者彌增其困，懼非所以欲均之意。

translations.literal: If the present system is then carried out, the rich man's goods and wealth will double of themselves, and the poor man's distress will increase all the more; I fear this is not the intent of wishing to equalize.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan proceeds, the rich will double their wealth and the poor grow poorer—I fear that is not equalizing intent.

sentences.zh: 又錢之形式，大小多品，直云大錢，則未知其格。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the form of money, large and small have many grades; to say simply large coin is not to know its standard.
translations.idiomatic: Coins come in many sizes; to say only "large coin" leaves the standard unknown.

sentences.zh: 若止於四銖五銖，則文皆古篆，既非下走所識，加或漫滅，尤難分明，公私交亂，爭訟必起，此最是其深疑者也。

translations.literal: If it stops at four-zhu or five-zhu, then the inscriptions are all ancient seal script, which common folk do not recognize; moreover some are worn away and especially hard to distinguish; public and private will mingle in disorder and lawsuits will surely arise—this is the deepest doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If limited to four or five zhu, the legends are ancient seal script unknown to common folk, often worn away and hard to read; public and private trade will tangle and lawsuits multiply—this is my deepest doubt.

sentences.zh: 命旨兼慮翦鑿日多，以至消盡；

translations.literal: The command also considers that clipping and chiseling grow daily until extinction;
translations.idiomatic: Your command also fears clipping will daily increase until coins vanish;

sentences.zh: 鄙意復謂殆無此嫌。

translations.literal: my humble thought again says there is probably no such worry.
translations.idiomatic: yet I think that worry is probably groundless.

sentences.zh: 民巧雖密，要有蹤跡，且用錢貨銅，事可尋檢，直由屬所怠縱，糾察不精，致使立制以來，發覺者寡。

translations.literal: Though the people's craft is secret, there must be traces; moreover using money means copper goods, a matter that can be traced and inspected; it is simply because the subordinate offices were lax and surveillance was not precise, causing since the system was established few to be discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Though folk are clever, they leave traces; coin is copper and can be traced. Lax enforcement and poor inspection, not the law itself, explain why few culprits have been caught.

sentences.zh: 今雖有懸金之名，竟無酬與之實，若申明舊科，禽獲即報，畏法希賞，不日自定矣。

translations.literal: Now though there is the name of suspended gold, in the end there is no reality of reward and payment; if the old statutes are clarified and capture is immediately rewarded, fearing the law and hoping for bounty, in no long time it will settle of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards are promised but not paid; if old statutes were enforced and captures rewarded at once, fear of law and hope of bounty would soon end the trouble.

sentences.zh: 愚者之議，智者擇焉，猥參訪逮，敢不輸盡。」

translations.literal: The foolish man's debate—the wise man chooses from it; I rudely join the inquiry and dare not fail to offer all."
translations.idiomatic: The wise choose among foolish counsel; invited to debate, I dare offer all I can."

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書庾炳之、侍中太子左衛率蕭思話、中護軍趙伯符、御史中丞何承天、太常郗敬叔並同尚之議。

translations.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Yu Bingzhi, Palace Attendant and Left Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent Xiao Sihua, Central Guard Commander Zhao Bofu, Imperial Censor He Chengtian, and Minister of Rites Xi Jingshu all agreed with Shangzhi's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yu Bingzhi, Attendant and Left Guard Leader Xiao Sihua, Central Guard Zhao Bofu, Censor He Chengtian, and Minister of Rites Xi Jingshu all sided with Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 中領軍沈演之以為：「龜貝行於上古，泉刀興自有周，皆所以阜財通利，實國富民者也。

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Shen Yanzhi held: "Tortoise shells and cowries circulated in high antiquity; knife-money arose from Zhou onward—all are means to enrich goods and open profit, truly making the state solid and the people rich.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Commander Shen Yanzhi argued: "Shell currency ruled antiquity and knife-money arose in Zhou—all to enrich trade and strengthen state and people.

sentences.zh: 歷代雖遠，資用彌便，但採鑄久廢，兼喪亂累仍，糜散湮滅，何可勝計。

translations.literal: Though dynasties were far apart, use grew ever more convenient; but mining and casting had long been abandoned, and with repeated chaos and ruin, scattering and extinction cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Though ages passed, coin grew more convenient; yet minting long ceased, and repeated chaos scattered and destroyed coin beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 晉遷江南，疆境未廓，或土習其風，錢不普用，其數本少，為患尚輕。

translations.literal: When Jin moved south of the Yangzi, the borders were not yet broad; in some regions custom kept to local ways and money was not universally used; the number was originally few and the harm still light.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin moved south, borders were narrow, local custom prevailed, coin was not universal, and scarcity did little harm.

sentences.zh: 今王略開廣，聲教遐暨，金鏹所布，爰逮荒服，昔所不及，悉已流行之矣。

translations.literal: Now the royal plan is open and broad, fame and teaching reach far; where metal currency is spread, it extends even to barbarian garb; what formerly did not reach has all now circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal domain is vast, civilization reaches far, and coin circulates even among distant tribes where it never reached before.

sentences.zh: 用彌廣而貨愈狹，加復競竊翦鑿，銷毀滋繁，刑禁雖重，姦避方密，遂使歲月增貴，貧室日虛，暋作肆力之氓，徒勤不足以供贍。

translations.literal: Use grew broader while goods grew narrower; moreover competing theft, clipping, and chiseling, destruction ever more frequent; though punishments were heavy, wicked evasion grew secret; thus years made goods dearer, poor households daily emptier; violent laborers toiled in vain, their toil not enough to support provision.
translations.idiomatic: Use spread while goods grew scarce; clipping and illicit minting multiplied; though punishments were heavy, crime grew cunning; years made goods dearer and poor households emptier, and laborers toiled without enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 誠由貨貴物賤，常調未革，弗思釐改，為弊轉深，斯實親教之良時，通變之嘉會。

translations.literal: Truly because goods were dear and things cheap, regular taxes were not reformed; not thinking to rectify and change, harm turned deeper—this is truly a fine time for close instruction and a splendid occasion for adapting change.
translations.idiomatic: Goods grew dear because taxes were not reformed and change was not sought; harm deepened—this is the right moment for reform.

sentences.zh: 愚謂若以大錢當兩，則國傳難朽之寶，家贏一倍之利，不俟加憲，巧源自絕，施一令而眾美兼，無興造之費，莫盛於茲矣。

translations.literal: My foolish view is that if one large coin equals two, then the state transmits hard-to-decay treasure, households win double profit, without waiting for added statutes craft cuts itself off, one order and all beauties combined, no cost of construction—nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If one large coin equals two, the state gains durable treasure, households double profit, craft dies without new laws, one order brings many gains, and no minting cost—nothing better.

sentences.zh: 」上從演之議，遂以一錢當兩，行之經時，公私非便，乃罷。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed Yanzhi's argument; thereupon one coin equaled two; it was carried out for a time; public and private found it inconvenient, and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Yanzhi; one coin was made equal to two; after a time public and private alike found it inconvenient, and the measure was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷左僕射，領汝陰王師，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Left Vice Director, concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Ruyin, his Regular Attendant status as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five he was made Left Vice Director and tutor to the Prince of Ruyin, retaining attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，轉尚書令，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight he became Secretariat Director and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，致仕，於方山著退居賦以明所守，而議者咸謂尚之不能固志，太子左衛率袁淑與尚之書曰：「昨遣修問，承丈人已晦志山田，雖曰年禮宜遵，亦事難斯貴，俾疎、班、邴、魏，通美於前策，龔、貢、山、衛，淪慚乎曩篇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he retired from office; at Fang Mountain he wrote the Rhapsody on Retired Dwelling to clarify what he upheld; but debaters all said Shangzhi could not hold firm to his will; Left Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent Yuan Shu wrote to Shangzhi: "Yesterday I sent to inquire after your health and learned that you, elder, have hidden your will in mountain fields; though one says age and ritual should be followed, the affair is hard and thus precious—Bi, Ban, Bing, and Wei spread their beauty in former records; Gong, Gong, Shan, and Wei sink in shame in past chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine he retired and wrote at Fang Mountain a rhapsody on retirement to declare his resolve; critics said he could not hold firm. Left Guard Leader Yuan Shu wrote: "Yesterday I inquired after you and learned you have hidden your will in the hills. Age and ritual counsel retirement, yet the act is hard and noble—Bi, Ban, Bing, and Wei shine in former records, while Gong, Gong, Shan, and Wei blush in past chapters.

sentences.zh: 規迨休告，雪滌素懷，冀尋幽之歡，畢棲玄之適。

translations.literal: I planned to await your rest and leave report, to cleanse my plain heart in snow, hoping to seek the joy of the hidden and complete the comfort of dwelling in mystery.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to wait your leave, cleanse my plain heart, seek hidden joys, and complete my dwelling in mystery.

sentences.zh: 但淑逸操偏迥，野性瞢滯，果茲沖寂，必沈樂忘歸。

translations.literal: But Shu's withdrawn conduct is eccentric and remote, and wild nature muddled and stagnant; if this quiet emptiness is realized, I shall surely sink in joy and forget return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my withdrawn bent is eccentric and my wild nature dull; if this quiet emptiness comes, I shall sink in joy and forget to return.

sentences.zh: 然而已議塗聞者，謂丈人徽明未耗，譽業方籍，儻能屈事康道，降節殉務，舍南瀕之操，淑此行永決矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who have already heard the talk on the road say that you, elder, still have bright emblem undiminished and fame and achievement just recorded; if you could bend to serve the healthy Way, lower your dignity and die for duty, abandon the conduct of the southern bank—then Shu's journey this time is forever decided.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rumor says your brilliance is undimmed and fame still fresh; if you bend to serve the Way, lower your dignity for office, and abandon the southern bank—then my journey is forever decided.

sentences.zh: 望眷有積，約日無誤。

translations.literal: I look to your regard with accumulation; fix the day without error.
translations.idiomatic: I look to your regard; let us fix a day without fail.

sentences.zh: 」尚之宅在南澗寺側，故書云「南瀕」，毛詩所謂「于以採蘋，南澗之瀕」也。

translations.literal: " Shangzhi's residence was beside Nanjian Temple; hence the letter says "southern bank"—what the Mao Odes call "To gather duckweed, at the southern bank of Nanjian."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi lived beside Nanjian Temple; hence the letter's "southern bank," from the Mao Odes: "To gather duckweed, at the southern bank of Nanjian."

sentences.zh: 詔書敦勸，上又與江夏王義恭詔曰：「今朝賢無多，且羊、孟尚不得告謝，尚之任遇有殊，便未宜申許邪。

translations.literal: Edicts earnestly urged him; the emperor also sent an edict to the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Now morning worthies are not many, and Yang and Meng still cannot request leave; Shangzhi's appointment and treatment are special—is it then not fitting to grant his request?
translations.idiomatic: Edicts urged him on; the emperor also wrote Prince Yigong of Jiangxia: "Worthy men are few today, and Yang and Meng still cannot retire; Shangzhi's treatment is special—should his request not be granted?

sentences.zh: 」義恭答曰：「尚之清忠貞固，歷事唯允，雖年在懸車，而體獨充壯，未相申許，下情所同。

translations.literal: " Yigong replied: "Shangzhi is pure, loyal, steadfast, and firm; in successive service he is only fitting; though his years are at the hanging chariot, his body alone is full and strong; not to grant his request is what lower sentiment shares.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong replied: "Shangzhi is pure, loyal, and steadfast; his service has always been fitting; though his years counsel retirement, his body remains strong; not to grant him is what all below wish.

sentences.zh: 」尚之復攝職。

translations.literal: " Shangzhi again assumed duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi resumed office.

sentences.zh: 羊即羊玄保，孟即孟顗，字彥重，平昌安丘人。

translations.literal: Yang is Yang Xuanbao; Meng is Meng Yan, courtesy name Yanchong, a man of Anqiu in Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang is Yang Xuanbao; Meng is Meng Yan, styled Yanchong, from Anqiu in Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 兄昶貴盛，顗不就徵辟。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chang was noble and flourishing; Yan did not accept summons or recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chang was powerful; Yan would not accept office.

sentences.zh: 昶死後，起家為東陽太守，遂歷吳郡、會稽、丹陽三郡，侍中，僕射，太子詹事，復為會稽太守，卒官，贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After Chang died, he began his career as Administrator of Dongyang, then successively held the three commanderies Wu, Kuaiji, and Danyang, Palace Attendant, Vice Director, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, again Administrator of Kuaiji; he died in office and was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang died he entered office as Administrator of Dongyang, then served Wu, Kuaiji, and Danyang, became Attendant, Vice Director, and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, again Administrator of Kuaiji, died in office, and was posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子劭，尚太祖第十六女南郡公主，女適彭城王義康、巴陵哀王休若。

translations.literal: His son Shao married Emperor Taizong's sixteenth daughter, the Princess of Nan Commandery; his daughter was married to the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and the Lamented Prince of Baling Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao married the emperor's sixteenth daughter, Princess of Nan Commandery; his daughter married Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Prince Xiuruo of Baling.

sentences.zh: 尚之既還任事，上待之愈隆。

translations.literal: Once Shangzhi had returned to his duties, the emperor treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shangzhi returned to office, the emperor treated him with still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 是時復遣軍北伐，資給戎旅，悉以委之。

translations.literal: At that time armies were again sent north to campaign; supplies for the military host were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were again sent north; supply for the campaign was wholly entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，進位司空，領尚書令。

translations.literal: When the prime culprit usurped the throne by regicide, Shangzhi was advanced to Minister of Works and held concurrently the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince murdered his father and seized the throne, Shangzhi was made Minister of Works and Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 時三方興義，將佐家在都邑，劭悉欲誅之，尚之誘說百端，並得免。

translations.literal: At that time the three regions raised righteous armies; the generals' and aides' families were in the capital; Shao wished to execute them all; Shangzhi persuaded by a hundred paths and all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: As the three regions rose in revolt, officers' families were in the capital; Shao wished to execute them all; Shangzhi argued by every means and saved them.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，復為尚書令，領吏部，遷侍中、左光祿大夫，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, Shangzhi again became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, held concurrently the Civil Service, was transferred to Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and held concurrently the post of Protector Army General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Shangzhi again became Secretariat Director, headed the Civil Service, was made Attendant and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and commanded the Protector Army.

sentences.zh: 尋辭護軍，加特進。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned the Protector Army and was given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned the Protector Army command and was given Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領尚書令。

translations.literal: He again with his former office held concurrently the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again held Secretariat Director with his existing titles.

sentences.zh: 丞相南郡王義宣、車騎將軍臧質反，義宣司馬竺超民、臧質長史陸展兄弟並應從誅，尚之上言曰：「刑罰得失，治亂所由，聖賢留心，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Chief Minister the Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan and Campaigning Chariots and Cavalry General Zang Zhi rebelled; Yixuan's Chief Clerk Zhu Chaomin and Zhi's Chief Clerk Lu Zhan and his brothers all should follow in execution; Shangzhi submitted a memorial, saying: "The gain and loss of punishments is what order and chaos come from; sages and worthies keep their hearts on it and cannot be incautious.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Prince Yixuan of Nan Commandery and Campaigning Chariots General Zang Zhi rebelled; Yixuan's chief clerk Zhu Chaomin and Zhi's chief clerk Lu Zhan and his brothers were all marked for death. Shangzhi memorialized: "Whether punishments hit or miss is the root of order and chaos; sages watch it closely and dare not be careless.

sentences.zh: 竺超民為義宣司馬，賊既遁走，一夫可禽，若反覆昧利，即當取之，非唯免愆，亦可要不義之賞，而超民曾無此意，微足觀過知仁。

translations.literal: Zhu Chaomin was Yixuan's Chief Clerk; once the rebels had fled, a single man could be captured; if he turned back for hidden profit he should at once be taken—not only escaping fault but also able to demand reward for unrighteousness—yet Chaomin never had this intent, slightly enough to observe fault and know benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chaomin was Yixuan's chief clerk. After the rebels fled, one man could have been seized; had he turned back for secret gain he should have been taken—not only to escape guilt but to claim reward for treachery—yet Chaomin never harbored such intent, enough to read his fault and see his humanity.

sentences.zh: 且為官保全城府，謹守庫藏，端坐待縛。

translations.literal: Moreover as an official he preserved the city walls and government offices, carefully guarded the storehouses, and sat upright awaiting binding.
translations.idiomatic: As an official he preserved the city, guarded the stores, and sat waiting to be bound.

sentences.zh: 今戮及兄弟，與向始末無論者復成何異。

translations.literal: Now execution extending to brothers—how is it again different from those who from first to last had no connection?
translations.idiomatic: Now to execute his brothers as well—how is that different from punishing men who had nothing to do with the affair from start to finish?

sentences.zh: 陸展盡質復灼然，便同之巨逆，於事為重。

translations.literal: Lu Zhan's full assistance to Zhi was clearly evident; to treat him the same as great rebels is heavy in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhan's aid to Zhi was plainly evident; to treat him as a great rebel is a weightier matter.

sentences.zh: 臣豫蒙顧待，自殊凡隸，苟有所懷，不敢自默。

translations.literal: Your servant has beforehand received regard and treatment, distinct from common subordinates; if I have something in my breast, I dare not keep silent myself.
translations.idiomatic: I have long received Your Majesty's regard, beyond common service; having thoughts in mind, I dare not keep silent.

sentences.zh: 」超民坐者由此得原。

translations.literal: " Those implicated with Chaomin were thereby pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Those implicated with Chaomin were thereby pardoned.

sentences.zh: 時欲分荊州置郢州，議其所居。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to divide Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, debating where it should be seated.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to split Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, and debated where the new seat should lie.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭以為宜在巴陵，尚之議曰：「夏口在荊、江之中，正對沔口，通接雍、梁，實為津要，由來舊鎮，根基不易。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held that it should be at Baling; Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies in the midst of Jing and the Yangzi, directly facing the mouth of the Mian, connecting Yong and Liang—it is truly a ford of vital importance, an old garrison from of old whose foundations are not easily changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia argued for Baling; Shangzhi said: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangzi, facing the Han mouth and linking Yong and Liang—a vital crossing and an old garrison whose foundations should not be lightly moved.

sentences.zh: 今分取江夏、武陵、天門、竟陵、隨五郡為一州，鎮在夏口，既有見城，浦大容舫。

translations.literal: Now taking the five commanderies Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui as one province, with the garrison at Xiakou, there is already an existing city and the harbor is large enough to hold ships.
translations.idiomatic: Take Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui as one province with the seat at Xiakou—there is already a city, and the harbor can hold large ships.

sentences.zh: 竟陵出道取荊州，雖水路，與去江夏不異，諸郡至夏口皆從流，並為利便。

translations.literal: From Jingling the route out to Jingzhou, though by waterway, is no different from going to Jiangxia; all commanderies reaching Xiakou follow the current—all are convenient.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingling the water route to Jingzhou is no longer than that to Jiangxia; all commanderies can reach Xiakou downstream—altogether convenient.

sentences.zh: 湘州所領十一郡，其巴陵邊帶長江，去夏口密邇，既分湘中，乃更成大，亦可割巴陵屬新州，於事為允。

translations.literal: The eleven commanderies led by Xiangzhou—among them Baling borders the long Yangzi and is close to Xiakou; having divided central Xiang, it becomes all the larger; Baling may also be cut off to belong to the new province—fitting in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou's eleven commanderies include Baling on the Yangzi, close to Xiakou; having split central Xiang, that province grows too large—Baling may be attached to the new province, which fits the plan.

sentences.zh: 」上從其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 荊、揚二州，戶口半天下，江左以來，揚州根本，委荊以閫外，至是並分，欲以削臣下之權，而荊、揚並因此虛耗。

translations.literal: The two provinces Jing and Yang held half the empire's households; since the east of the Yangzi, Yangzhou was the root foundation and Jing was entrusted with the outer gate; at this point both were divided, wishing thereby to pare the power of ministers and subjects, yet Jing and Yang both thereby grew empty and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yang together held half the realm's population; since the move east of the Yangzi, Yang had been the root and Jing the outer gate—now both were split to curb ministers' power, and both provinces were drained thereby.

sentences.zh: 尚之建言復合二州，上不許。

translations.literal: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi urged reuniting the two provinces; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，以為左光祿、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Grandee of the State with the Protocol of the Three Dukes; his Palace Attendant status remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 he was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grandee of the State with protocol equal to the Three Dukes, retaining his attendant title.

sentences.zh: 尚之在家常著鹿皮帽，及拜開府，天子臨軒，百僚陪位，沈慶之於殿廷戲之曰：「今日何不著鹿皮冠？

translations.literal: Shangzhi at home often wore a deerskin cap; when he was invested as Grandee of the State, the Son of Heaven came to the hall, the hundred officials attended in place, and Shen Qingzhi in the court hall jested with him, saying: "Why not wear the deerskin cap today?
translations.idiomatic: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap. At his investiture as Grandee, the emperor came to the hall and the officials attended; Shen Qingzhi jested in court: "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?

sentences.zh: 」慶之累辭爵命，朝廷敦勸甚篤，尚之謂曰：「主上虛懷側席，詎宜固辭。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi repeatedly declined enfeoffment and appointment; the court earnestly urged him with great sincerity; Shangzhi said to him: "The sovereign empties his breast and sits sidewise—how could one firmly decline?
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi had repeatedly declined honors while the court urged him earnestly. Shangzhi told him: "The sovereign waits with open mind—how can you refuse so firmly?

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「沈公不効何公，去而復還也。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi said: "Master Shen does not imitate Master He—leave and then return again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "Master Shen does not follow Master He's example—leave and then come back again.

sentences.zh: 」尚之有愧色。

translations.literal: " Shangzhi had a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 愛尚文義，老而不休，與太常顏延之論議往反，傳於世。

translations.literal: He loved and upheld literary meaning; old yet he did not rest; with Minister of Rites Yan Yanzhi he debated back and forth, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He loved letters and never ceased in old age; his exchanges with Minister of Rites Yan Yanzhi circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 立身簡約，車服率素，妻亡不娶，又無姬妾。
