translations.literal: In standing he was simple and restrained; carriage and dress were generally plain; when his wife died he did not marry again, and he had no concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, with plain carriage and dress; after his wife died he did not remarry and kept no concubines.

sentences.zh: 秉衡當朝，畏遠權柄，親戚故舊，一無薦舉，既以致怨，亦以此見稱。

translations.literal: Holding the balance in the court, he feared and kept distant from power; kin and old friends—he made not a single recommendation; both thereby drawing resentment and also thereby winning praise.
translations.idiomatic: Holding power in court, he shunned nepotism and recommended no kin or friend—winning resentment, but also praise.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領中書令。

translations.literal: He again with his former office held concurrently Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He again held Secretariat Director with his existing titles.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾篤，詔遣侍中沈懷文、黃門侍郎王釗問疾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his illness was grave; an edict sent Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year four his illness grew grave; the emperor sent Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 薨于位，時年七十九。

translations.literal: He died in office; he was seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空，侍中、中書令如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Works; Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, retaining attendant and Secretariat Director titles.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡穆公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jian-mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke Jian-mu.

sentences.zh: 子偃，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Yan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 尚之弟悠之，義興太守，侍中，太常。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's younger brother Youzhi was Administrator of Yixing, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's younger brother Youzhi was Administrator of Yixing, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 與琅邪王微相善，悠之卒，微與偃書曰：「吾與義興，直恨相知之晚，每惟君子知我。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Wei of Langye; when Youzhi died, Wei wrote to Yan: "I and Yixing—I only regret knowing each other late; I always think the gentleman understands me.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wang Wei of Langye. When Youzhi died, Wei wrote to Yan: "With Yixing I regret only that we met so late; I always felt he understood me as a gentleman should.

sentences.zh: 若夫嘉我小善，矜余不能，唯賢叔耳。

translations.literal: As for praising my small goodness and pitying my inability—only your worthy uncle.
translations.idiomatic: As for praising my small virtues and pitying my failings—that was your worthy uncle alone.

sentences.zh: 」悠之弟愉之，新安太守。

translations.literal: " Youzhi's younger brother Yuzhi was Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's younger brother Yuzhi was Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 愉之弟翌之，都官尚書。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's younger brother Yizhi was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's younger brother Yizhi was Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 悠之子顒之，尚太祖第四女臨海惠公主。

translations.literal: Youzhi's son Yongzhi married Emperor Taizong's fourth daughter, the Lamented Princess of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's son Yongzhi married the emperor's fourth daughter, the Lamented Princess of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，官至通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he reached the post of Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he rose to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江左以來，樹根本於揚越，任推轂於荊楚。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Since the east of the Yangzi, they planted root and foundation in Yang and Yue and entrusted the pushing of the chariot wheel to Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Since the court moved east of the Yangzi, it rooted itself in Yang and Yue and entrusted the chariot's push to Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 揚土自廬、蠡以北，臨海而極大江；

translations.literal: Yang territory from Lu and Li northward faces the sea and reaches the great Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: Yang territory ran from Lu and Li northward to the sea and the great Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 荊部則包括湘、沅，跨巫山而掩鄧塞。

translations.literal: Jing region then embraced Xiang and Yuan, crossed Witch Mountain and covered Deng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jing embraced Xiang and Yuan, crossed Witch Mountain, and covered Deng Pass.

sentences.zh: 民戶境域，過半於天下。

translations.literal: Households and territory exceeded half of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Their households and territory exceeded half the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉世幼主在位，政歸輔臣，荊、揚司牧，事同二陝。

translations.literal: In the Jin age a young lord held the throne and government returned to assisting ministers; the governors of Jing and Yang were affairs like the two Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, child emperors left government to regents; the governors of Jing and Yang stood like the two Shaan.

sentences.zh: 宋室受命，權不能移，二州之重，咸歸密戚。

translations.literal: When the Song house received the Mandate, power could not be shifted; the weight of the two provinces all returned to close kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Song received the Mandate, power could not shift; the weight of both provinces fell to close kin.

sentences.zh: 是以義宣藉西楚強富，因十載之基，嫌隙既樹，遂規問鼎。

translations.literal: Thus Yixuan relied on western Chu's strength and wealth, took advantage of a decade's foundation, and once resentment and rifts were planted, then schemed to inquire of the tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yixuan, relying on western Chu's wealth and a decade's foundation, once rifts arose, plotted to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 而建郢分揚，矯枉過直，藩城既剖，盜實人單，閫外之寄，於斯而盡。

translations.literal: Yet establishing Ying and dividing Yang bent the crooked past the straight; once the barrier cities were cut apart, the thief's substance was a single man; the trust of the outer gate ended at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet founding Ying and splitting Yang overcorrected the fault; once the great provinces were carved up, the outer gate was left thin, and trust in frontier power ended there.

sentences.zh: 若長君南面，威刑自出，至親在外，事不患強。

translations.literal: If a mature lord faces south, authority and punishment issue from himself; close kin are outside—affairs need not fear strength.
translations.idiomatic: When a mature ruler holds the throne, authority issues from him; with close kin kept outside, strength need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 若運經盛衰，時艱主弱，雖近臣懷禍，止有外憚，呂宗不競，實由齊、楚，興喪之源，於斯尤著。

translations.literal: If fortune passes through flourishing and decline, the times are hard and the lord weak—even if near ministers harbor disaster, they only have outer fear; the Lü clan did not contend, truly because of Qi and Chu; the source of rise and fall is especially clear here.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune turns and the throne is weak, even treacherous courtiers fear the outer provinces; the Lü clan failed because Qi and Chu stood firm—the source of rise and fall shows clearly here.

sentences.zh: 尚之言并合，可謂識治也矣。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's words on reuniting may be called understanding governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's plea to reunite the provinces shows true understanding of governance.
